status: active microrevision chain; Phoenix direct target readings unresolved
central_claim: The 1833 first print and 1857 Selections both directly preserve 'caste' in the physiognomic phrase, while 1857 also preserves 'seventy years ago'. Thus both later corrections occur after long-lived published readings. A near-contemporary 1875 review independently establishes that Phoenix reprints incorporated Hodgson's marginalia from his own earlier printed copies and fed the 1874 collected edition.

microchains.secure_result: The simple restoration model is false: 1833/1857 preserve 70, while the later sequence contains at least 70 -> some -> about 100.
microchains.active_breakpoint: Phoenix determines whether 70 -> some entered serial print before the 1874 collected edition.

microchains.secure_result: The 1874 cast correction is not a restoration of the 1833 printed reading. Caste persisted for at least four decades in the published tradition before the explicit correction to cast.
microchains.active_question: The 1832 manuscript is still needed to determine whether cast restores an unpublished manuscript reading or is a genuinely late semantic revision.

transmission_model: fair manuscript -> first print -> 1857 reprint -> author marginalia on printed copy -> Phoenix serial text -> 1874 collected base -> printed correction apparatus -> copy-specific manuscript annotation branches -> selective later reprint
source_control_rules: Do not promote predicted Phoenix readings to direct readings.
The 1875 review establishes transmission direction but not diplomatic identity of every word.
Do not call cast a restoration until the 1832 manuscript is read, even though it is demonstrably not the 1833 printed reading.
Keep edition-level and copy-specific states separate.
Treat digital scan existence, text accessibility, and direct reading as separate evidence states.
